question.text: An IPEV-aligned valuer applies a 'discount to the quoted market ratio' when valuing an unlisted investee using listed-peer multiples. What does this discount primarily reflect, and when may it be reduced?

answer.text: Reflects tax-gross-up; reduced when LTCG rates fall
Reflects currency risk; reduced when INR appreciates
Reflects credit risk; reduced when issuer is rated AAA
Reflects illiquidity / lack of marketability of unlisted stock; may be reduced if the fund manager believes an exit is imminent

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 14.8.3 point 3, IPEV Multiples Approach: 'it is normal to apply a discount to the quoted market ratio to reflect illiquidity discount applicable to unlisted stock. This discount may be reduced if a fund manager believes an exit to be imminent.' The discount captures the absence of a public trading window. The Trap: Credit/tax/FX risks are separate adjustments, not the DLOM reason. Cross-Exam Context: XV (RA) and XXI-B (PM) know DLOM conceptually. XIX-C demands the 'imminent exit' reduction — a manager-specific judgement call that materially impacts end-of-fund NAV. Manager's Pro-Tip: When marking up an investee on imminent exit, reduce DLOM in a stepped manner (25% -> 15% -> 5% -> 0%) tied to hard signposts (signed LOI, SPA draft, regulator filing). A sudden one-step drop to zero signals valuation aggression and triggers auditor scrutiny.
